policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV "and cometh into the borders of Judaea and beyond the Jordan" coordinates the two regions with "and" (καί); RP's διὰ τοῦ πέραν would make the Jordan region the route travelled through, which the ASV does not render.
ASV "And there came unto him Pharisees, and asked him" renders the participle and subject προσελθόντες Φαρισαῖοι explicitly; the shorter base leaves the subject unexpressed.
Imperfect ἐπηρώτων and aorist ἐπηρώτησαν are both rendered by ASV "asked"; the English aspect does not distinguish them.
Both readings say "Moses suffered"; only Greek word order and the Μωϋσῆς/Μωσῆς spelling differ, neither of which English word order or "Moses" reflects.
ASV "But Jesus said unto them" has no rendering of RP's ἀποκριθείς ("answering"), and "But" answers the base δέ.
ASV "Male and female made he them" leaves the subject in the verb; RP's added ὁ θεός would give an explicit "God made them", which the ASV does not print.
ASV prints "and shall cleave to his wife" in the text, and the mapped textual_variant note ("Some ancient authorities omit and shall cleave to his wife") assigns the omission to the margin.
ASV "And in the house" renders either preposition; Mark's εἰς with a verb of remaining is regularly Englished "in", so the locative ἐν is not required.
ASV "the disciples asked him again of this matter" renders περὶ τούτου; RP's αὐτοῦ περὶ τοῦ αὐτοῦ would give "his disciples" and "of the same", neither of which the ASV has.
Imperfect and aorist of ἐπερωτάω are both "asked" in ASV; nothing in the English distinguishes them.
ἄν and ἐάν in the relative clause are alike rendered by ASV "Whosoever"; the particle has no separate English exponent.
ASV "if she herself shall put away her husband, and marry another" renders αὐτή and the active γαμήσῃ ἄλλον; RP's γυνή would give "a woman" and the passive γαμηθῇ ἄλλῳ "be married to another".
Only the order of pronoun and verb differs; ASV "that he should touch them" fixes English order regardless.
ASV "the disciples rebuked them" takes the children as object; RP's τοῖς προσφέρουσιν would give "rebuked those that brought them".
ἄν and ἐάν are both covered by ASV "Whosoever"; the English has no exponent for the particle.

ASV "blessed them, laying his hands upon them" puts the blessing before the laying on of hands, excluding RP's order with εὐλόγει after; the remaining readings differ only in the augment spelling κατευλόγει/κατηυλόγει, which English cannot show.
ASV "Do not kill, Do not commit adultery" has killing first, excluding the Treg/RP order; the two remaining readings differ only in punctuation.
ASV "And he said unto him" renders a bare verb of speaking with no "answering", excluding both ἀποκριθείς readings.
ἕν σε ὑστερεῖ and ἕν σοι ὑστερεῖ are alike "One thing thou lackest"; the case of the pronoun leaves no English trace.
The article with πτωχοῖς is required in English either way: ASV "give to the poor" would stand with or without τοῖς.
ASV "and come, follow me" has no rendering of RP's ἄρας τὸν σταυρόν ("taking up the cross"), and prints nothing italicized in its place.

ASV prints "for them that trust in riches" in the text, and the mapped textual_variant note ("Some ancient authorities omit for them that trust in riches") puts the shorter base reading in the margin.
ASV "a needle's eye" renders either articular or anarthrous Greek; English article usage here is fixed by the idiom, not by τῆς.
ASV "to go through a needle's eye" renders διελθεῖν; RP's εἰσελθεῖν would give "to enter", which the ASV reserves for the kingdom clause following.
ASV text reads "saying unto him" (πρὸς αὐτόν), and the mapped textual_variant note "Many ancient authorities read among themselves" assigns ἑαυτούς to the margin.
ASV begins "Jesus looking upon them saith" with no connective; RP's added δέ would be rendered by the "And/But" the ASV uses everywhere else in this chapter for that particle.
ASV "all things are possible with God" must supply a copula in English whether or not ἐστιν stands in the Greek.
Only the order of ὁ Πέτρος and λέγειν differs; ASV "Peter began to say unto him" is fixed English order either way.
ASV "have followed thee" parallels its "have left" for the aorist ἀφήκαμεν, so the perfect/aorist difference in ἠκολουθήκαμεν is not distinguished by the English.
ASV "Jesus said" renders a single verb of speaking with no "answering", excluding ἀποκριθεὶς ... εἶπεν.
ASV "or mother, or father, or children" has mother before father and no "wife"; RP's πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ἢ γυναῖκα differs in both.
ASV "and mothers" is plural, rendering μητέρας rather than Treg's singular μητέρα.
ASV "and the last first" requires the English article by idiom whether or not οἱ stands in the Greek.
ASV "and they that followed were afraid" treats the participle as a substantive subject, rendering the article οἱ; RP's anarthrous καὶ ἀκολουθοῦντες gives the circumstantial "as they followed".
ASV "the chief priests and the scribes" would carry "the" by English idiom with or without τοῖς.
ASV "shall spit upon him, and shall scourge him" has spitting before scourging, the base order; RP reverses the two verbs.
ASV "shall kill him" needs an English object regardless, and the pronoun is carried over from the preceding clauses; the added αὐτόν leaves no distinguishing trace.
ASV "after three days" renders μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας; RP's τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ would give "on the third day".
ASV "the sons of Zebedee" has no "two", which WH's added δύο would require.
ASV "saying unto him, Teacher" renders the dative αὐτῷ with the participle, which RP omits.
ASV "whatsoever we shall ask of thee" renders the object σε, which RP lacks.
ASV "What would ye that I should do for you?" renders subjunctive and infinitive constructions alike, and the "I" is required by English whether or not με stands in the Greek.
Only the position of σου within the phrase differs; ASV "one on thy right hand" is the same English either way.
ἀριστερῶν and εὐωνύμων are both "left hand" in ASV, and the "thy" in "on thy left hand" is the natural English repetition of the earlier σου, so RP's added σου is not distinguished.
ASV "or to be baptized with the baptism" renders the disjunctive ἤ rather than RP's connective καί.
RP's added μέν has no English exponent; the ASV clause "The cup that I drink ye shall drink" reads the same with or without it.
ASV "on my right hand or on my left hand" renders the disjunctive ἤ, not RP's καί.
The readings differ in connective (καί/δέ) and in the position of ὁ Ἰησοῦς; ASV "And Jesus called them to him" renders δέ as "and" as freely as καί, and English word order is fixed either way.
ASV "But it is not so among you" is present tense, rendering ἐστιν; RP's ἔσται would give "shall not be so".
ἄν and ἐάν are alike absorbed into ASV "whosoever would become great".
Only the order of μέγας and γενέσθαι differs; ASV "would become great" is fixed English order.
ἄν and ἐάν are alike absorbed into ASV "whosoever would be first".
ASV "first among you" renders the prepositional ἐν ὑμῖν; the Treg and RP readings have the genitive ὑμῶν, which would give "first of you".
ASV "the son of Timaeus" requires the English article by idiom whether or not ὁ stands in the Greek.
ASV "Bartimaeus, a blind beggar" is an indefinite appositive, rendering anarthrous τυφλός; RP's ὁ τυφλός would give the definite "the blind man" as the ASV renders it later in v. 49.

ASV "a blind beggar, was sitting by the way side" renders the noun προσαίτης before the verb, excluding the NIV/RP reading with the participle προσαιτῶν after "by the way"; the remaining readings are the same words.
ASV renders both Ναζαρηνός and Ναζωραῖος as "the Nazarene", so the English does not distinguish the two forms.
The vocative Υἱέ and the nominative-for-vocative ὁ υἱός are both "thou son of David" in ASV.
ASV "and said, Call ye him" quotes a direct imperative; RP's αὐτὸν φωνηθῆναι is indirect and would give "commanded him to be called".
ἔγειρε and ἔγειραι are alike "rise" in ASV; the imperative form leaves no English trace.
ASV "sprang up" renders ἀναπηδήσας; RP's ἀναστάς is the ordinary "rose/arose" the ASV uses elsewhere in this chapter (v. 1).
ASV "And Jesus answered him, and said" is past tense with the participle ἀποκριθείς; RP's present λέγει αὐτῷ would give the historic "saith unto him", as the ASV renders that verb in vv. 11, 27, 42.
Only Greek word order differs; ASV "What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?" is the same English either way.
ASV "And straightway he received his sight" renders καὶ ὁ or ὁ δέ alike, since the ASV freely gives δέ as "and".
εὐθύς and εὐθέως are both "straightway" in ASV.
ASV "and followed him in the way" renders the pronoun αὐτῷ; RP's τῷ Ἰησοῦ would give the name "Jesus".
